item.title: Vindication Swim w/ Q&A | Additional Films and Guests — Mon Nov 9, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Vindication Swim tells the remarkable story of Mercedes Gleitze, who in 1927 became the first British woman to swim the English Channel. Facing press hostility, anti-immigrant bias, and constraints on women in sport, Mercedes’ achievement remains a powerful testament to her grit, courage, and determination. Writer-director Elliott Hasler—only 23 when the film premiered—pursued period authenticity through grassroots collaboration with coastal communities throughout the UK. Three years in the making, the film’s swimming sequences were shot miles out in the Channel, vividly capturing the perils of Mercedes’ epic crossing. [98 min; drama; English]
A Q&A with director Elliott Hasler and Radhika Parameswaran (Herman B Wells Endowed Professor, Media School) will follow the screening.
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Nov 10 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Nov 10 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Nov 10 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Tue Nov 10, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop — Tue Nov 10, 6:00 PM — Global & International Studies Building
item.description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.
It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.
Instructions:
Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session
If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop.
If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.

item.title: Fall 2026 Packing Party — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — Cedar Hall - C102
item.description:
This is our biggest event that takes place in the fall semester and once in the spring semester. During this event, we get together to create Pretty Packages, our care packages that we give to women fighting cancer. These packages consist of things like the trademark Fighting Pretty boxing gloves representing empowerment, skincare and makeup products to remind these women of their inner and outer beauty, a handwritten note from each of our Fighting Pretty members, and more. We personally deliver these packages to these women at the IU Health Hospital at a later date, and from past experience, we have seen how much of an impact this truly makes for these strong women. This event is open to members of the club and prospective members looking to join the club.
Hosted by: Fighting Pretty at Indiana University
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12966827
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: Yaga, Episdoes 1 - 4 — Wed Nov 11, 8:00 PM
item.description:
The story follows a gritty private investigator named Rapp (Noah Reid) and a local police detective named Carson (Clark Backo) as they probe the mysterious disappearance of Henry Park, the heir to a wealthy commercial fishing family in the misty coastal town of Whittock. As they dig deeper, their investigation uncovers local secrets, dark witchcraft, a campus professor named Katherine (Carrie-Anne Moss), and modern reimaginings of the Slavic folklore myth of Baba Yaga.
Source: The Back Door

item.title: Navigating the Workplace — Thu Nov 12, 5:00 PM — IMU Solarium
item.description: Navigating the Workplace is a professional development event hosted by the Indiana University Black Student Union designed to prepare Black students for the realities of entering and succeeding in professional environments where they may be underrepresented. The event will feature a panel discussion with Black alumni and industry professionals who will share their experiences, challenges, and strategies for navigating workplace dynamics, addressing bias and discrimination, advocating for themselves, and maintaining their authenticity in professional settings. Following the panel, attendees will participate in an interactive workshop focused on practical skills such as workplace communication, professional boundaries, documentation, networking, and career advancement. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Nov 16 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Nov 16 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: Embedded Counseling (CAPS) — Mon Nov 16, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
Supporting your well-being is an important part of our work at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. That's why we are proud to partner with Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS) to provide an embedded counselor in our space every Monday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mollibeth Penner, LHMCA serves as our embedded counselor and works directly with students connected to the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. To schedule an appointment, please call CAPS (https://healthcenter.indiana.edu/make-appointment/index.html) and let them know you are an LGBTQ+ Culture Center student interested in meeting with Mollibeth at the center. We hope this partnership makes it easier for you to access support in a space where you feel comfortable and affirmed. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.
Source: IU LGBTQ+ Culture Center

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Mon Nov 16, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Fri Nov 20, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Nov 21 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past
